messages.author: 8b81798616f7af4b
messages.subject: Monitored nodes in particle filter
parts:
Hi,

is it possible to monitor multiple nodes in a state space model using buildBootstrapFilter()? 

For example, if I'm using a linear transition function in order to model a system's kinematic behaviour (e.g. for tracking an object's position), I can estimate the position, velocity and acceleration in a a 3-d matrix, something similar too: 

x[1:3, t] ~ dmnorm(A %*% x[1:3, t-1] , prec = Λ)

where A is:

A <- matrix(c(1, dt, 0.5*dt^2,
              0, 1, dt,
              0, 0, 1),
            nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)

and x[1,t] is the position, x[2,t] is the velocity and x[3,t] is the acceleration.

But is it possible to use individual nodes for the state variables, and to monitor these individually?

cheers,
Andrew

messages.author: 5938cc942c6238be
messages.subject: Re: Monitored nodes in particle filter
parts:
Hi Andrew,

Particle filters in NIMBLE will always monitor all of the latent states, there is currently no way to specify only a subset of latent states for monitoring (although that's a good idea!)  

As for using individual nodes for latent state variables, I'm not quite sure if this is what you want, but it could be helpful: for a given time point t, the particle filters in NIMBLE are able to handle state variables that are specified individually in BUGS code.  For example, in a state space model with two latent states at each time, one could specify the two state variables as coming from two different distributions by:

x[1, t] ~ dnorm(a * x[1, t-1], sd = 1)
x[2, t] ~ dt(b * x[2, t-1], sigma = 5, df  = 1)

The only catch is that all of the latent variables at time t, whether specified individually or as coming from a multivariate distribution, have to be elements of the same vector (in this example, x[ , t]).  Also in this example, to build a bootstrap filter, I think you would also have to give the argument:

control = list(timeIndex = 2)

to the buildBootstrapFilter() function.  This argument lets the filter know that the second dimension of the x[ , ] matrix is the dimension that indexes time.  Please let me know if this wasn't clear, thanks!

Nick

messages.subject: Re: Monitored nodes in particle filter
parts: Ahh that makes sense.  In NIMBLE, elements of a multivariate distribution all have to come from the same vector, so that if you want the position, velocity, and acceleration to be drawn at each time t from a MVN distribution, they will have to be elements of the same vector (i.e. x[1:3, t]).  However, it would be possible to create deterministic nodes that represent position, velocity, and acceleration at time t in BUGS code using:
x[1:3, t] ~ dmnorm(A %*% x[1:3, t-1] , prec = Λ)

position[t] <- x[1, t]
velocity[t] <- x[2, t]
acceleration[t] <- x[3, t]

Currently we don't have a system in place to monitor these deterministic nodes in a particle filter (which is what I think you would like), but I think this could be added pretty quickly if it would be useful!  

As a less elegant but quicker solution (and you may already have something like this in place), you could extract samples from the bootstrap filter after it has been run using either 
 
pfSamples <- as.matrix(cBootstrapFilter$mvWSamples, 'x')       for non-equally weighted samples, or
pfSamples <- as.matrix(cBootstrapFilter$mvEWSamples, 'x')     for equally weighted samples,

where "cBootstrapFilter" is whatever name you have given the compiled bootstrap filter algorithm that you have built and run.  Then you could use something like 

colnames(pfSamples) <- gsub('x\\[1, ', 'position\\[', colnames(pfSamples))
colnames(pfSamples) <-gsub('x\\[2, ', 'velocity\\[', colnames(pfSamples))
colnames(pfSamples) <-gsub('x\\[3, ', 'acceleration\\[', colnames(pfSamples))

to replace the column names for easier access.

messages.author: 5938cc942c6238be
messages.subject: Re: Monitored nodes in particle filter
parts:
You're welcome Andrew.  You are correct that the bootstrap filter currently returns the log of the normalized weights.  I can see how having the ESS and/or unnormalized weights would be a nice feature to have though.  I modified the bootstrap filter a little bit so that this information should now be accessible.  The slightly modified bootstrap filter is available here:

https://nature.berkeley.edu/~pdevalpine/nimbleExamples/filtering_bootstrapESS.R

If you source the filtering_bootstrapESS.R file after loading NIMBLE in an R session, the modified algorithm should work by calling buildBootstrapFilterV2(), and will take all the same arguments as the original buildBootstrapFilter() function.  The two differences in buildBootstrapFilterV2() are:
  1. The mvWSamples model values object that can be accessed after the bootstrap filter has been run now has separate columns for the log normalized weights, labeled "normWts", and the log unnormalized weights, labeled "unnormWts"
  2. After running the bootstrap filter, you can now call the "returnESS()" method to return the ESS values for each time point.  For example, if you had a compiled bootstrap filtering algorithm named "cMyBootstrapFilter", then:
cMyBootstrapFilter$run(10000)
cMyBootstrapFilter$returnESS()

would return the ESS values from the cMyBootstrapFilter object

Hopefully this is useful - please let me know if you find any bugs in this modified algorithm or if you have any other ideas for filtering features that aren't currently implemented.  Thanks!

Nick

On Tuesday, April 11, 2017 at 7:43:38 PM UTC+2, Nicholas L. Michaud wrote:
Ahh that makes sense.  In NIMBLE, elements of a multivariate distribution all have to come from the same vector, so that if you want the position, velocity, and acceleration to be drawn at each time t from a MVN distribution, they will have to be elements of the same vector (i.e. x[1:3, t]).  However, it would be possible to create deterministic nodes that represent position, velocity, and acceleration at time t in BUGS code using:

x[1:3, t] ~ dmnorm(A %*% x[1:3, t-1] , prec = Λ)
position[t] <- x[1, t]
velocity[t] <- x[2, t]
acceleration[t] <- x[3, t]

Currently we don't have a system in place to monitor these deterministic nodes in a particle filter (which is what I think you would like), but I think this could be added pretty quickly if it would be useful!  

As a less elegant but quicker solution (and you may already have something like this in place), you could extract samples from the bootstrap filter after it has been run using either 
 
pfSamples <- as.matrix(cBootstrapFilter$mvWSamples, 'x')       for non-equally weighted samples, or
pfSamples <- as.matrix(cBootstrapFilter$mvEWSamples, 'x')     for equally weighted samples,

where "cBootstrapFilter" is whatever name you have given the compiled bootstrap filter algorithm that you have built and run.  Then you could use something like 

colnames(pfSamples) <- gsub('x\\[1, ', 'position\\[', colnames(pfSamples))
colnames(pfSamples) <-gsub('x\\[2, ', 'velocity\\[', colnames(pfSamples))
colnames(pfSamples) <-gsub('x\\[3, ', 'acceleration\\[', colnames(pfSamples))

to replace the column names for easier access.

On Monday, April 10, 2017 at 6:26:30 PM UTC+2, Nicholas L. Michaud wrote:
Hi Andrew,

Particle filters in NIMBLE will always monitor all of the latent states, there is currently no way to specify only a subset of latent states for monitoring (although that's a good idea!)  

As for using individual nodes for latent state variables, I'm not quite sure if this is what you want, but it could be helpful: for a given time point t, the particle filters in NIMBLE are able to handle state variables that are specified individually in BUGS code.  For example, in a state space model with two latent states at each time, one could specify the two state variables as coming from two different distributions by:

x[1, t] ~ dnorm(a * x[1, t-1], sd = 1)
x[2, t] ~ dt(b * x[2, t-1], sigma = 5, df  = 1)

The only catch is that all of the latent variables at time t, whether specified individually or as coming from a multivariate distribution, have to be elements of the same vector (in this example, x[ , t]).  Also in this example, to build a bootstrap filter, I think you would also have to give the argument:

control = list(timeIndex = 2)

to the buildBootstrapFilter() function.  This argument lets the filter know that the second dimension of the x[ , ] matrix is the dimension that indexes time.  Please let me know if this wasn't clear, thanks!

Nick
